NOT FOR SUBMIT — will be dropped') is being added to _build-and-test.yml, which is the single shared source of truth for BOTH CI lanes AND the Gerrit Verified gate; if merged it runs on the real pre-merge gate and must be reverted before submit.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether the integration tier step also needs the faulthandler-timeout/step-timeout instrumentation, or confirm the hang is scoped to the default suite.
evidence: _build-and-test.yml:452-456 the integration step run block has no --faulthandler-timeout and the step has no timeout-minutes
_build-and-test.yml:447-451 integration tier runs concurrency + reconciler (subprocess/xdist loadgroup) tests
advisory.finding: The instrumentation is applied only to the default suite step; the integration tier step (subprocess-heavy concurrency/reconciler tests, an equally plausible hang candidate) received neither `timeout-minutes` nor `--faulthandler-timeout`, so a hang there is undiagnosed and can still idle the job.
scenarios: The hang is actually in an integration test; the diagnostic step never runs it and the integration step still idles.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Apply the same timeout-minutes / --faulthandler-timeout instrumentation to the integration-tier pytest lane (line 446) if the hang could originate there.
evidence: Default suite step gets the instrumentation: `timeout-minutes: 60` (line 423) and `--faulthandler-timeout=900` (line 442)

Integration lane has no timeout/faulthandler: `- name: Run the integration tier (concurrency + reconciler; network-guarded)` ... `pytest -m integration -n ... --dist loadgroup -q -p no:cacheprovider --durations=25 --basetemp=...` (lines 446-456)

scenarios: The CI hang originates in the integration tier rather than the default suite

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider a job-level timeout-minutes on the `test` job so hangs in any step are bounded, not just the default-suite step.
evidence: Job header with no timeout-minutes: `  test:` / `    name: pytest (${{ matrix.os }}, py${{ matrix.python-version }})` / `    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}` (lines 190-192)
The only timeout-minutes in the file is the newly-added step-level one: `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:423: timeout-minutes: 60` (search_files)
advisory.finding: The `test` job has no job-level timeout-minutes, so any un-instrumented step (e.g. the integration lane) can still hang up to GitHub's 360-minute default before the runner is reclaimed.
scenarios: A step other than the instrumented default-suite step hangs; the job burns runner minutes toward the 360-min default

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify the hang occurs within a test's call phase (not teardown/collection/worker shutdown) or add a session-level watchdog, since --faulthandler-timeout only covers per-test execution.
evidence: Commit body: 'name the test that hangs CI lanes at 99% (orphaned git children ...)'
_build-and-test.yml:419-422 comment: faulthandler 'dumps every thread's stack when any single test exceeds 900s, naming the hung test'
--faulthandler-timeout is per-test; a hang outside a test's call phase (teardown/collection/worker shutdown) is not covered
dropped.finding: The stated hang is 'orphaned git children ... at 99%'; `--faulthandler-timeout=900` only arms during a test's execution phases, so a hang in collection, session teardown, or xdist worker shutdown would not trigger a faulthandler dump and `timeout-minutes: 60` would kill the job with no stack — defeating the diagnostic's goal of naming the hung test.
scenarios: Hang occurs during xdist worker shutdown or fixture teardown at end of run; faulthandler never fires, job is killed at 60m with no traceback.
